gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Heavy and bold, Plakkaat bends its lines like straw, terminals curling nearly back to the stem. Noto Sans Old North Arabian stands tall and dense beside it, with outward-pointing ends like tongs, open where the heading closes.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Noto Sans Old Permic reads friendly and current, its rounded forms staying open to the side and its small letters nearly matching the capitals. And Plakkaat, heavy and bent-straw bold, never thins into calligraphic strokes, so the two feel boldly different in how they are drawn.

Heavy, bent-wire lettering up top, with every curve as thick as a straight stem, then a lofty, breathing body below. Plakkaat hits hardest as a display voice; Noto Sans Old Persian is the plain sans that lets the text open up.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-sog: Noto Sans Old Sogdian reads clean and approachable, its tall x-height nearly touching cap height and its wide mouths staying crisp when small. Plakkaat earns its keep big and short, where its closed, heavy shapes land.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Thick, uniform bars and a heavy swagger. Plakkaat does its loudest work large, while Noto Sans Old Turkic, with chunky tall lowercase and open-mouthed curves, is happiest given a modest size beneath it.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Plakkaat leads with bold, heavy letters whose terminals sweep around to nearly touch the stem. Noto Sans Oriya replies with generous gaps in its curves and small letters almost as tall as the capitals, so closed and open forms trade places.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage reads friendly and businesslike, its lowercase bowls puffed out like inflated shapes and its sweeping curves never closing. Plakkaat, heavy and closed above, hands over to this plain sans for paragraphs that feel generous and unhurried.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Plakkaat looks drawn with a single pen tip, heavy and bent like straw with a low capital-to-body contrast. And Noto Sans Osmanya gives it a clean foil, its s shapes turning wide and easy while its lowercase looms large beside the capitals.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Wire-bent heaviness against a high-set, gapped body. Plakkaat does its best work as a bold display voice whose s curves never thin; Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong, a neutral sans-serif, handles the quieter text.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-palmyre: Plakkaat's lettering looks drawn with one pen tip, heavy and bent, with terminals sweeping nearly shut against the stem. Noto Sans Palmyrene stays open beneath it, curves stopping short, ascenders compressed, a sans-serif foil.
